question: According to the manual, studies show that nearly a third of all fatally injured motorcycle riders had BAC levels:
choice_a: Impossible to measure with modern equipment
explanation: Studies show that nearly a third of all fatally injured motorcycle riders had BAC levels above the legal limit of 0.08%, and an additional 8% had lower levels (0.01 to 0.07%), showing that just a drink or two can impair riding skills.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.38, 'Why This Information is Important'

question: Compared with automobile crashes, substance abuse is involved in what proportion of motorcycle crashes according to the manual?
choice_a: 90% of motorcycle crashes, versus 33% of automobile crashes, involve abuse of substances
choice_b: Substance abuse is equally rare in both types of crashes
choice_c: Substance abuse is involved in more automobile crashes than motorcycle crashes
choice_d: The manual states substance abuse plays no measurable role in motorcycle crashes
explanation: Motorcyclists are more likely to be killed or severely injured in a crash than automobile drivers. Injuries occur in 90% of motorcycle crashes and 33% of automobile crashes that involve abuse of substances.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.38, 'Why This Information is Important'

question: How quickly does alcohol enter the bloodstream compared to most foods and beverages?
choice_a: Alcohol takes hours to be absorbed, longer than most food
choice_b: Alcohol does not need to be digested and reaches the brain within minutes
choice_c: Alcohol has no measurable effect on the brain
choice_d: Absorption speed depends only on the time of day
explanation: Unlike most foods and beverages, alcohol does not need to be digested. Within minutes after being consumed, it reaches the brain and begins to affect the drinker.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.39, 'Alcohol in the Body'

question: According to the manual, what three primary factors determine Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC)?
choice_a: Only body weight matters -- amount and speed of drinking are irrelevant
choice_b: Time of day, distance to be ridden, and helmet type
choice_c: The amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight
choice_d: Engine displacement, tire pressure, and weather
explanation: Three primary factors play a major part in determining BAC: the amount of alcohol you consume, how fast you drink, and your body weight.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.39, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration'

question: A 12-ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with 1.5 ounces of hard liquor, and a 5-ounce glass of wine:
choice_a: Only hard liquor is significant enough to affect BAC
choice_b: Beer always contains far more alcohol than wine
choice_c: Wine always contains far more alcohol than beer
choice_d: All contain the same amount of alcohol
explanation: A 12-ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with one shot (1.5 ounces) of hard liquor, and a 5-ounce glass of wine all contain the same amount of alcohol.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.39, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration'

question: Approximately how fast can alcohol be eliminated from the body?
choice_c: Instantly, with no elimination time needed
choice_d: Only after eight hours of sleep, regardless of amount
explanation: Generally, alcohol can be eliminated from the body at the rate of almost one drink per hour, though a variety of factors -- sex, physical condition, food intake -- may cause BAC to remain higher.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.39, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration'

question: In most states, what BAC level is considered legally intoxicated for an adult operator?
choice_d: There is no defined legal threshold
explanation: In all but one state, an adult with a BAC of 0.08% or above is considered intoxicated. A breath, blood, or urine test determines whether an operator is riding legally.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.39-40, 'Alcohol and the Law'

question: Is impairment of judgment and riding skill limited to riders who are legally intoxicated?
choice_a: Impairment only begins after the legal limit is exceeded by double
choice_b: Yes, skills are unaffected until the legal limit is reached
choice_c: No -- impairment of judgment and skills begins well below the legal limit
choice_d: Impairment applies only to skills testing, not actual riding
explanation: Whether or not you are legally intoxicated is not the real issue -- impairment of judgment and skills begins well below the legal limit.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.40, 'Alcohol and the Law'

question: As a rider's ability to judge their own performance is affected by alcohol, what illusion does the manual describe?
choice_a: There is no known effect on self-assessment
choice_b: Riders become more cautious and self-aware as they drink
choice_c: Riders always become drowsy immediately after one drink
choice_d: Although the rider is performing more and more poorly, they believe they are doing better and better
explanation: Your ability to judge how well you are riding is affected first -- although you may be performing more and more poorly, you think you are doing better and better, resulting in greater and greater risk-taking.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.40, 'Minimize the Risks'

question: What does the manual identify as the single most effective way to make an intelligent choice about drinking and riding?
choice_a: Don't drink -- once you start, your resistance is weaker
choice_b: Set a strict personal drink limit and stick to it exactly
choice_c: Only drink beer instead of hard liquor
choice_d: Drink only on a full stomach
explanation: Don't Drink -- once you start, your resistance is weaker. Setting a limit or pacing yourself are poor alternatives at best, since judgment is one of the first things affected by alcohol.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.40, 'Make an Intelligent Choice'

question: What does the manual suggest doing to protect a friend who has had too much to drink?
choice_a: Let them ride slowly and carefully on their own
choice_b: Arrange a safe ride, slow their pace of drinking, and keep them there with food and conversation
choice_c: Avoid saying anything, since it is not your responsibility
choice_d: Give them coffee and send them on their way immediately
explanation: To keep friends from hurting themselves: arrange a safe ride, slow the pace of drinking, keep them there with food and conversation, get other friends involved, and if possible take their key and secure their bike.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.40-41, 'Step In to Protect a Friend'

question: Even where cannabis is legal for medicinal or recreational use, the manual states that operating a motor vehicle while impaired by it is:
choice_a: Only a concern for passengers, not operators
choice_b: Completely legal and poses no risk
choice_c: Still not legal, safe, or wise, since it distorts perception of time, space, and speed
choice_d: Safer than riding after drinking alcohol
explanation: Although cannabis may be legal for medicinal or recreational use in your state, it is still not legal, safe, or wise to operate a motor vehicle while impaired by cannabis, since it distorts perception of time, space and speed.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.41, 'Cannabis & Motorcycle Operation'

question: How can the duration of cannabis impairment differ depending on how it is consumed?
choice_a: Smoking cannabis always produces longer impairment than eating it
choice_b: Method of consumption has no effect on onset or duration
choice_c: Eating cannabis eliminates any riding impairment
choice_d: When eaten, onset can be delayed over an hour and the high can last more than 6 hours, versus effects beginning within minutes and lasting 2-4 hours when smoked
explanation: When cannabis is smoked, effects generally begin within a few minutes and can last 2 to 4 hours. When eaten, onset could be delayed more than an hour, and the duration of the high could be more than 6 hours.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.41, 'Cannabis & Motorcycle Operation'

question: According to the manual, how does riding a motorcycle compare with driving a car in terms of fatigue on a long trip?
choice_a: Riding a motorcycle is more tiring, so a rider will tire sooner than in a car
choice_b: Riding a motorcycle is far less tiring than driving a car
choice_c: There is no difference in fatigue between the two
choice_d: Fatigue only affects passengers, not operators
explanation: Riding a motorcycle is more tiring than driving a car. On a long trip you'll tire sooner than you would in a car, and fatigue can affect your control of the motorcycle.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.41, 'Fatigue'

question: According to the manual, experienced riders seldom try to ride more than about how many hours in a day?
choice_d: There is no recommended daily limit
explanation: Limit your distance -- experienced riders seldom try to ride more than about six hours a day, and should take frequent rest breaks, stopping at least every two hours.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.41, 'Fatigue'
